agent_summary:
Lane 74 (Information gathering) against juice.lab.test — confirmed OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0 (Angular SPA served by nginx/1.30.5 reverse-proxying a Node.js/Express ^4 backend on localhost:3000, Sequelize REST models, socket.io, Prometheus, LLM chatbot gemma4:e4b). Only http answers; https/443 refused. All 10 WSTG-INFO items were performed read-only and have evidence.

Surface covered (120 HTTP requests): metafiles (robots.txt→/ftp, sitemap=SPA catch-all, security.txt), the SPA index + main.js (full route/endpoint map), static bundles and all lazy chunks, /metrics, /.well-known/csaf (+index.txt, changes.csv), /ftp directory and files, and the documented /api/{Model}s and /rest/* endpoints. Access control was mapped: collection GETs for Products/Feedbacks/SecurityQuestions/Deliverys/Recycles/Quantitys are public while item-level and user/admin endpoints (Users, Cards, Addresss, BasketItems, SecurityAnswers, Complaints, basket, order-history, b2b, 2fa, saveLoginIp, authentication-details) return 401/403. Hidden-parameter test on /rest/products/search returned byte-identical responses (no extra params read). Guessed sensitive paths (.git/config, .env, de.json, uploads/) return the 9393-byte SPA catch-all (not exposed).

Leads recorded for a human to validate: (high) /ftp/incident-support.kdbx KeePass DB downloads directly (200 octet-stream) bypassing the .md/.pdf allowlist that 403s the .bak files; (medium) /rest/memories exposes user records incl. password hashes/tokens/emails unauthenticated; (low) verbose Express stack traces leak absolute source paths and framework version; (low) unauthenticated /metrics exposes runtime internals; (low) /rest/user/security-question?email= enables account enumeration; (low) HTTP-only with wildcard CORS and no HSTS/CSP. 

Nothing was left open. Limitation: the run's display budget was exhausted after ~x25, so later response bodies were not rendered to me (statuses/headers and gateway redaction flags were used, and full bodies are retained as evidence); no writes were attempted (read-only engagement).

leads.title: [agent] KeePass database incident-support.kdbx downloadable unauthenticated from /ftp

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/ftp/incident-support.kdbx returns 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream and Content-Length 3246 (matching the /ftp listing), so the KeePass password database downloads directly without authentication. This bypasses the fileServer .md/.pdf allowlist that returned 403 for package.json.bak. An attacker could crack the KDBX offline to recover stored credentials.

leads.title: [agent] No HTTPS listener and missing transport/CSP security headers

detail.text: The host answers only on http:// (port 443 refused connection). Responses carry x-frame-options, x-content-type-options and feature-policy, but no Strict-Transport-Security and no Content-Security-Policy header were observed on any response, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin is wildcard (*). Traffic including session tokens would traverse cleartext HTTP.

GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op returns 200 with a JSON body (134 bytes) describing the account's security question. An unauthenticated caller can probe arbitrary emails to learn whether an account exists and which security question it uses.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated /rest/memories exposes user records (password hashes, tokens, emails)

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/memories returns 200 (6183 bytes) without any session. The response embeds author User objects; the gateway redacted 26 sensitive values flagged as password, deluxeToken and email address, indicating password hashes/tokens and email addresses of users are disclosed to anonymous callers via the photo-wall memories endpoint.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics endpoint exposes runtime internals

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/metrics returns 200 with full Prometheus metrics (no auth, no security headers). Leaks process CPU/memory (process_resident_memory_bytes, heap), open fds, startup task timings, HTTP status-code counts, and LLM token counters. Useful for recon/architecture mapping and could aid resource monitoring of the host.

leads.title: [agent] Verbose error stack traces leak internal paths and framework version

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/ftp/package.json.bak returns 403 with a full HTML stack trace: "OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.22.1)" and absolute server paths like /juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:68 and /juice-shop/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js. Discloses framework/version, directory layout and source file names. The /ftp fileserver also restricts downloads to .md/.pdf (confirming an allowlist).
